title: Financial consolidation: what it is, how it works, and what to check
summary: Financial consolidation combines a parent and its subsidiaries into one set of figures. See what is eliminated and when it is still not ready for the board.
body_markdown:
# Financial consolidation: what it is, how it works, and what to check


**Financial consolidation presents a parent and its subsidiaries as a single economic entity.** Assets, liabilities, equity, income, expenses, and cash flows come into one set of statements, after removing what moved only inside the group.


Add the balance sheets without that removal and the group looks larger than it is. A sale from one legal entity to another in the same group becomes revenue on one side and cost on the other. A receivable sits next to the payable for the same transaction. The board, the bank, and the auditor do not read that sum. They read the position of the group.


In a group with subsidiaries, a holding company, and cost shared across operations, the balance sheet can close in the system while the caveat stays in a spreadsheet. This guide covers what financial consolidation is, what[CPC 36 (R3)](https://conteudo.cvm.gov.br/export/sites/cvm/menu/regulados/normascontabeis/cpc/CPC_36_R3_rev_08.pdf) , the Brazilian standard aligned with IFRS 10, requires, and the check that separates a number that is on time from a number that is ready for the board.


## What financial consolidation is


Consolidated financial statements are the statements of the economic group. The parent and its subsidiaries appear as if they were a single entity. Each company keeps its own legal personality, ledger, and separate statements. Financial consolidation is prepared from those statements. It does not create a new company, and it does not compute the group's tax.


What is included is what the parent controls. Under the standard, control combines three elements: power over the investee, exposure to variable returns, and the ability to use that power to affect those returns. An ownership percentage helps show the power. On its own, it is not the test.


An associate and a joint arrangement do not follow the same path. Significant influence and joint control have their own treatment, generally the equity method, in the standards that cover those investments. Calling every group total financial consolidation mixes situations the standard keeps apart.


## A sum, tax consolidation, and a cash consolidation


Three similar phrases answer different questions.


What it answers What it does with an internal transaction


Sum of the companies What each legal entity has, side by side Leaves the transaction counted twice


Financial consolidation What the group's position is Removes what moved only inside the perimeter


Tax consolidation How tax is computed Follows the rules of the tax regime


Cash consolidation How much the group has available Gathers balances, without building the group balance sheet


A sum is the wrong starting point for a board decision. It inflates revenue, cost, assets, and liabilities by the amount of the internal transaction. Profit may not change, if the margin has already left the group, but the size of the lines does. Anyone reading leverage or margin on a sum is reading a group that does not exist.


Tax consolidation is a different object. It is a tax computation regime, with its own rules. Cash consolidation is different too: it answers how much is available, not what the group's equity is. Each company's[financial close](https://www.abstra.io/en/articles/fechamento-financeiro-continuo) comes first. Financial consolidation uses those books. It does not replace them.


## How financial consolidation works


The accounting work has four movements. The order matters, because adding figures before defining the perimeter brings in a company that should not be there.


1. **Define the perimeter for the period.** Which companies the parent controls that month. An acquisition, a sale, and a loss of control change the tree and have to be reviewed at the close, not copied from the previous month.
2. **Align policies before adding.** Accounting policies, the chart of accounts, and the presentation currency have to agree. Different policies for the same transaction cannot be added raw.
3. **Aggregate line by line.** Assets, liabilities, equity, income, expenses, and cash flows of the parent and the subsidiaries form the group's position.
4. **Eliminate what is internal.** The parent's investment is removed against the corresponding portion of the subsidiary's equity. Balances, income, expenses, and cash flows between companies in the perimeter are removed, including profit that still sits in a group asset and has not been realized with a third party.


The result is a set of group statements, with notes on the basis, the subsidiaries, and the eliminations. It is not a parallel management report, and it does not, by itself, create a tax or corporate effect: tax and dividends are still computed in each company.


Elimination criteria, currency translation, and the ownership policy stay with the people who answer for the financial statements. A period check does not replace that judgment.


## A simple elimination example


The parent records 100 receivable from the subsidiary. The subsidiary records 100 payable to the parent. In a sum, the group shows an asset and a liability that do not exist outside it. In financial consolidation, the pair comes out.


If the parent sold at a margin and the inventory is still at the subsidiary, that margin is not the group's result either. It is realized only when the item leaves to a third party. While the inventory stays inside, the internal profit comes out of the consolidation.


The example is illustrative, with a round number. The point is the same in a real close: intercompany with no counterparty has no pair to eliminate. The balance stays in both books, or in only one, and the consolidated figures carry a caveat.


## Where financial consolidation stalls in practice


The standard describes what the set of statements has to contain. The close shows where the check slips out of the system. Three caveats repeat when the group grows and the process does not keep up:


- intercompany with no counterparty;
- a cost center that did not absorb the shared cost;
- an outdated corporate structure.


Intercompany without the other side blocks an elimination. A cost center that did not absorb leaves cost outside the operation that should carry it. An outdated structure makes the month use a tree that is no longer the group's.


While that lives on a sheet, the system can show a closed balance sheet and controllership keeps the true version beside it. The following month, nobody repeats the check the same way.


There is a second distinction, inside the queue itself. One item blocks an elimination. Another is only a document, such as a memo that still has no support. Treating both as the same pending item either hides the block or holds the close for an attachment.


## On time and ready for the board are not the same check


Closing on time answers whether the books for the period were closed. Being ready for the board answers what still keeps this number from being presented.


Check The question


Deadline Did the period close?


Structure Is the tree the one for that month?


Equation Do assets, liabilities, and equity sum to zero?


Queue What blocks an elimination, and what is only a document?


The four can diverge on the same day. The balance-sheet equation can be validated and the queue can still be named, with a company and an effect. Zero is not a stamp that the caveat disappeared. It is the condition for the round to be complete. The board needs both sentences: the consolidation closed, and this is still open.


## What Abstra does in this check


Abstra takes this check off the spreadsheet and puts the round in a single period. Receipt of the balances, the group tree, and absorption by cost center stop living in different files.


In practice, review and execution stay in the same flow:


- the round for one period is opened;
- the companies' balances enter that round;
- what is still open is counted separately;
- absorption arrives by cost center;
- what blocks an elimination stays separate from what is only a document;
- the round is complete only if assets, liabilities, and equity sum to zero, on that month's structure.


What has already been checked and what has not yet been absorbed stay together. Controllership stops rebuilding the story at month-end.


The round does not import a ledger from another system, does not calculate foreign exchange, and does not produce an opinion. It records the period, that month's structure, the absorption, and the queue of what still keeps the number from going to the board.


## Where to start


If your last close still ran this check outside the system, the next step is a thirty-minute conversation about one period that is already closed. With controllership. No product presentation.


Bring the sheet where the caveat stayed: intercompany, cost center, structure. The conversation is there to see what the round would keep in place of that sheet.


[Talk to Abstra about that period](https://www.abstra.io/en/talk-to-expert)


## Frequently asked questions


### What is financial consolidation?


Financial consolidation presents a parent and its subsidiaries as a single economic entity. Assets, liabilities, equity, income, expenses, and cash flows are combined after removing what moved only inside the group.


### Is financial consolidation the sum of the group companies?


No. A sum leaves the internal transaction counted on both sides. Financial consolidation removes that pair so the group does not look larger than it is.


### What is the difference between financial consolidation and tax consolidation?


Financial consolidation builds the group's financial statements. Tax consolidation is a tax computation regime, with its own rules. One does not replace the other.


### When is financial consolidation ready for the board?


When the period is closed, the structure used is that month's structure, assets, liabilities, and equity sum to zero, and the queue still says what blocks an elimination and what is only a document. The deadline alone does not answer this.


### Does a zero equation finish financial consolidation?


No. Assets, liabilities, and equity can sum to zero while the caveat stays named. Closing the number and being ready for the board are different checks.
